claims.text: In the CoT literature, checkability is the completeness and soundness of a verifier. In [Kirchner et al. 2024](./#p=kirchner2024proververifier), the prover "always generates correct and convincing solutions" and no "sneaky" prover from the same class of models can make the verifier accept an incorrect one. [Kim & Lee 2026](./#p=kim2026mitigating) require only that the verifier accept the prover's correct answers, but also that "there exists no adversarial proof that can trick the verifier into accepting an incorrect answer".

claims.reason: The sentence blends the two definitions and states each more weakly than its source. Kirchner et al.'s completeness requires the prover to always produce correct and accepted solutions, not only that the verifier accept correct ones. Kim & Lee's soundness is not limited to provers from the same model family: no incorrect proof at all may be accepted. Kim & Lee decouple correctness from checkability, so only Kirchner restricts the adversary to the model family.
